text:
### Observed differences

- The clearest difference sits at the branch after A37. In the earlier window, about 54 in 100 of A37's observed outgoing transitions led to A39 and about 46 in 100 to A38; in the later window this reversed, with about 54 in 100 leading to A38 and about 46 in 100 to A39. A37 itself appeared in every trace in both windows, so the shift lies in the branch choice, not in A37's occurrence. [DIR025, OCC024]
- Downstream, A38 appeared in about 60 in 100 traces before and about 69 in 100 after, and also repeated more often (traces containing a repeat: about 10 in 100 before, about 17 in 100 after; mean occurrences per trace about 0.77 versus 0.91), while A39 and A40 each fell from about 69 in 100 traces to about 59 in 100. [OCC025, OCC026, OCC027]
- A17 and A18, each present in roughly half of the traces, swapped prominence: A17 rose from about 44 to about 54 in 100 traces while A18 fell from about 57 to about 47. The outgoing shares around them moved too: from A17, the share continuing to A19 fell from about 32 to about 18 in 100 while the share going to A26 rose from about 44 to about 53; from A20, the share to A17 rose from about 17 to about 28 while the share to A18 fell; A19 slipped from about 50 to about 47 in 100 traces and A20 rose from about 50 to about 54. [OCC014, OCC015, OCC016, OCC017, DIR010, DIR012, DIR013]
- A30 and A31 each rose from about 46 to about 54 in 100 traces, while A32 and A33 each fell from about 55 to about 46; from A26 the outgoing share to A30 rose from about 19 to about 27 in 100 while the shares to A32 and A33 eased down, and the shares from A30 and A31 towards A27 evened out from about 58/42 to 50/50. [OCC018, OCC019, OCC020, OCC021, DIR016, DIR019, DIR020]
- Among A01, A03, A04 and A05, participation stayed near 50 in 100 traces in both windows, but the outgoing shares redistributed towards the stepwise route A01→A03→A04→A05: from A01 the share to A03 rose from about 28 to about 47 in 100; from A03 the share to A04 rose from about 27 to about 46 while the share to A09 fell from about 37 to about 21; from A04 the share to A03 fell from about 39 to about 20 while the share to A05 rose to about 40; from A05 the share to A04 fell from about 38 to about 28 while the share to A09 rose to about 39. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- A10 and A11 still appeared in every trace but repeated less often (traces with a repeat: about 43 in 100 before, about 35 in 100 after). [OCC009, OCC010]
- Most other tested activities and edges (for example A02, A06–A08, A13, A14, A16 and the near-even splits around A21–A22 and A28–A29) moved by at most about 2 in 100 with low empirical strength — the kind of difference two 200-trace samples of one process typically show. [OCC002, OCC006, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013, DIR002, DIR014, DIR017]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the choice at the branch point A37 shifted between two existing alternatives: in the earlier window the branch led more often to A39 (with A40 alongside it), in the later window more often to A38, while A37's own frequency stayed unchanged. The shift is measured directly on A37's outgoing shares with strong support (about 335 outgoing transitions per window) and an empirical strength of about 0.98, and it is matched in direction and size by the downstream participation changes — A38 up about 9 in 100 traces, A39 and A40 down about 9–10 in 100, with empirical strengths of about 0.92–0.94. All involved activities were well observed in both windows and only the shares between the alternatives moved, which fits a change in how often existing paths are taken, with a secondary element of A38 repeating more often within its traces. [DIR025, OCC024, OCC025, OCC026, OCC027]

Limitations: part of A38's increase is extra repetition rather than only more traces containing it, so the change is not purely a branch-share shift; A39 and A40 show identical values throughout, so the evidence cannot attribute the reduced path to one of them; and the evidence set contains no screening baseline, so the judgement rests on the directness and consistency of these measures rather than on a comparison with a chance expectation. An important competing explanation that cannot be ruled out is an internal change within the A38 path (for example the extra repetition) driving part of the shift rather than a re-weighing at A37 itself; the only internal measure of that path, its outgoing shares, changed only weakly. [OCC026, OCC027, DIR026]

Other differences:
- A17 rose from about 44 to about 54 in 100 traces while A18 fell from about 57 to about 47, with the outgoing shares of A17, A19 and A20 redistributing accordingly — a share shift between well-observed alternatives of the same kind as the main hypothesis. [OCC014, OCC015, OCC016, OCC017, DIR010, DIR012, DIR013]
- The A30/A31 group rose (each about 46 to about 54 in 100 traces) while the A32/A33 group fell (about 55 to about 46), with A26 routing more of its outgoing share to A30. [OCC018, OCC019, OCC020, OCC021, DIR016]
- Outgoing shares among A01, A03, A04 and A05 shifted towards the stepwise route while their participation stayed flat, suggesting the flow through that mesh follows the full sequence more often and the skips less often. [DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- A10 and A11 repeated somewhat less often while remaining present in every trace. [OCC009, OCC010]

These additional differences are not tied to the A37 branch shift by the evidence, which covers only activity participation and immediate successor shares and cannot show whether the changed paths involve the same traces or a shared trigger.
